nodes.rationale: Both directions are safe for the rules of spec 0003: a later timeline closes writes and no rule opens writes because of a timeline on a node in recovery; the exact replay timeline needs a replication connection and the REPLICATION attribute, which is too much for a monitor; scope 007 qualifies this on a real replica

nodes.label: Backend loss (spec 0004): when a read from or a write to the backend fails, the backend closes or it sends something that is not accepted, the session ends, POOL opens no new backend and sends nothing again (0001 SC-6); at a message boundary the client gets 08007 when a query is in flight and 08006 when none is; a query is in flight from the first byte of a Query written toward the backend until its ReadyForQuery was written to the client, so a COMMIT whose answer was lost gives 08007

nodes.label: Frontend authentication (spec 0004), six steps after a valid startup packet over TLS: POOL sends AuthenticationSASL with the one mechanism SCRAM-SHA-256 and never offers SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS (SEC-3); the client's SASLInitialResponse must start with n,, or y,, and a request for channel binding, an authorization identity or an extension is 08P01; POOL sends AuthenticationSASLContinue with the combined nonce (its own is 18 random bytes in base64), the salt and the count of the verifier; the final message must repeat the header and the whole nonce with a 32 byte proof; POOL compares the SHA-256 of the client key with the stored key in constant time and sends AuthenticationSASLFinal with the server signature; no match is 28P01; each authentication message is at most 1024 bytes and the whole exchange has the deadline limits.startup_timeout_ms

nodes.label: Startup (spec 0004): POOL reads the first 8 bytes of a new connection (a length and a code) with exact reads and no buffer in between; SSLRequest (80877103) is answered S before TLS and is 08P01 after TLS; GSSENCRequest (80877104) is answered N, allowed once before TLS; CancelRequest (80877102) is read, does nothing and closes with no answer; a StartupMessage of major version 3 is 28000 in plain text before TLS and is read and checked after TLS; any other major version is 0A000 and anything else 08P01

nodes.label: Startup packet rules of spec 0004: a length below 8 is 08P01 and a length above limits.startup_packet_max_bytes is 54000, both close the connection and the body is never read; a connection may send at most three first packets (an optional GSSENCRequest, then SSLRequest, then over TLS a StartupMessage or a CancelRequest) and any other order is 08P01; the TLS server offers TLS 1.3 and 1.2 with the defaults of rustls, asks for no client certificate and offers no ALPN protocol; direct TLS is not supported

nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m3 (observation.rs:140): a latest sample dated after now, or two samples tied at the latest time, count as no evidence, which hides a seen second primary on a node other than the writer; fix: a spec decision for scope 004 on the caller's duty
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: the smallest is a duty of the caller, written into the documentation comment of writer_admission and into Follow-up 4 (read now after the list of observations is fixed, pass at most one sample per node); a stricter one is in the rule itself: for a node other than the writer, a latest sample that cannot be used closes with a reason of its own.Both inputs can happen in scope 004 without anyone doing something strange: a probe result that lands a moment after the daemon read now is in the future of now, and two probe paths handing in the same sample tie. In both cases one admission can open while a second primary is in the list. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 28 (heavy, m1): a Ready state learns of a conflict latch set after the start through two functions of the state, latch_conflict (sets the latch in memory from a closed answer) and latch_recorded (takes the revision from a receipt only the journal can make), new AC-17; runner up: read and classify the journal again after every write

nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 28 (heavy, m1): a ready state learns of a conflict latch set after the start through two functions of the state, latch_conflict (sets the latch in memory from a closed answer) and latch_recorded (takes the revision from a receipt only the journal can make), new ac-17; runner up: read and classify the journal again after every write
nodes.rationale: The rule should not rest on a caller remembering to do something; the latch is set in memory first and the write follows, so that a slow disk cannot delay closing (from the cross check of spec 0004); a restart after a failed write forgets the latch, and a second primary that is still there is latched again at once

nodes.label: 0003 decision 29 (heavy, m3): the rule Fresh does not get stricter for a sample that cannot be used; one caller, build_snapshot, a board with one sample per node, a clamp of now and a guard on the name writer_admission, new AC-18; runner up: a new reason evidence.sample_unusable
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Authority Model: Startup States and Bootstrap
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 29 (heavy, m3): the rule fresh does not get stricter for a sample that cannot be used; one caller, build_snapshot, a board with one sample per node, a clamp of now and a guard on the name writer_admission, new ac-18; runner up: a new reason evidence.sample_unusable
nodes.rationale: AC-11 is pinned by assertions that expect an open answer when a node other than the writer has a latest sample from the future or two samples at the same time; a stricter rule would have changed accepted evidence; the cost is that the safety now has three parts and that the guard matches text, so a comment that holds the name writer_admission in another crate is refused too

nodes.label: 0003 decision 30 (heavy, m2): everyone inside pool-control and nobody outside may build a journal value; other crates get an opaque JournalRead and a source guard keeps StoredAuthority, StoreProbe, classify_startup and plan_bootstrap out of them, new AC-19; runner up: private fields and one constructor that runs the checks of the reader

nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 30 (heavy, m2): everyone inside pool-control and nobody outside may build a journal value; other crates get an opaque journalread and a source guard keeps storedauthority, storeprobe, classify_startup and plan_bootstrap out of them, new ac-19; runner up: private fields and one constructor that runs the checks of the reader
nodes.rationale: Private fields look stronger than a guard on a name and are not: whatever the tests use to build a journal value, other crates can use; the cross check of spec 0004 showed that guarding the one name StoredAuthority is not enough, so the daemon no longer holds a StoreProbe

nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 5 (heavy): a first start is told from a lost journal by an explicit bootstrap command plus the authority id repeated in the configuration as a witness; runner up: the explicit command alone
nodes.rationale: A daemon that finds an empty directory cannot know whether a journal ever existed; the configuration is the only other durable thing an operator controls, and the same value binds a configuration to its journal in both directions.

nodes.rationale: The three changes every test survived: skipping the expected_writer check for all clusters when one cluster has a bad id, running that check although a node has a bad cluster, and letting the endpoint check read a node whose port failed (AC-15 made input 3). Suggested fix: two clusters where one has a bad id and the other a wrong writer; a writer whose node has a bad cluster; two nodes with the same host and port = 0.These are the rules that make one mistake give one finding (AC-2). They were reworded after the verification of milestone 2, so they are the part of the validation order most likely to be touched again. Owner: the tester.

nodes.rationale: The recommendation is both, in two steps. The buffer removes one system call per finding and changes nothing a user can see, so it needs no decision; it bounds neither memory nor output size. A limit does, and it changes a public contract: AC-3 says the whole configuration is reported in one run, and a last line saying findings were left out is new output under spec 0001. So the user decides it, before the first start of the daemon in scope 004.

nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 24 (heavy): the system identifier, the authority id and the timeline id may appear in log fields and default diagnostics, never as metric labels, and the observed role may also be a label; runner up: never by default for the system identifier, [redacted] in debug
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not treat the system identifier as a secret (pg_control_system() returns it, IDENTIFY_SYSTEM answers with it), it is no credential, and it is the one value that explains an identity mismatch. Against: it names a cluster for its whole life and its upper bits hold the initialization time; neither opens a door. Redaction would cost a hand written Debug on every type that carries the number. Metric labels are held back because a label is copied onto every sample and often leaves the host.

nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: add the exception to PRD-006 AC-2, or a dated note under it that points to spec 0003, and say in the spec that rule 10 leaves quarantined nodes out on purpose, so that scope 010 knows the exception also covers a quarantined node on a later timeline.The document reviewer rated this major; the main reviewer rates it minor. The decision is written down and reasoned (decision 17, heavy) and judged right: the quarantine is the reviewed answer to exactly that node, closing would let one returned old primary stop a cluster after a correct promotion, and POOL sends nothing to the quarantined node either way. What is missing is one sentence where the requirement lives. docs/prd/ is not a file a sub session may change, so this is for the lead. Owner: the lead and the architect.

nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m1 (admission.rs:182, authority.rs:137): a ready state cannot learn of a conflict latch set after the start, so writes reopen once the second primary drops out of sight; fix: a spec 0003 decision before scope 004 plus a walk from row d to row o
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: decide it in spec 0003 before scope 004 dispatches SQL (a new item of Follow-up 4 or a criterion next to AC-16): either a pool-control function that takes a Ready state and a Closed that asks for the latch and returns the state with the latch set, or a rule that the daemon reads and classifies the journal again after every write, plus the memory for a failed write; then add a walk from row d to row o through the real functions, with the second primary gone in the second call.This is the case R-19 and PRD-006 AC-2 are about: the other primary is still there, it just cannot be seen any more, and writes open again. It is the same kind of gap as the one 0003 AC-16 closed, where the function trusted its caller. Nothing calls the function yet, so nothing is wrong today; it will be wrong on the first day of scope 004 unless that slice adds the missing piece inside pool-control. The same holds for the authority revision in an Open answer. Owner: the architect for the spec, then the developer.

nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Writer Admission and Conflict Evidence
nodes.rationale: Mutations are journaled with caller, idempotency key and expected generation so conflicting requests against one generation yield at most one effect; failure to persist intent prevents the external action.

nodes.label: Administration mutation retry contract
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Writer Admission and Conflict Evidence
nodes.rationale: Retries resolve by actor, action and request ID; the same request returns the original operation ID even after lost response or restart, and reuse with a different target or payload conflicts, so one accepted request yields one logical operation.

nodes.label: Restricted read only replica profile
nodes.rationale: Naive read detection can send side effects to a replica or break session and read after write semantics, so replica selection happens only inside explicit read only profiles and unsafe or uncertain operations are rejected.

nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m7 (cargo.toml:14): the workspace dependency pool-control is declared and taken by no member, so cargo 1.100.0 warns on every command, against the agents.md:31 rule; fix: take the line out until scope 004 adds the first use, or add a dated note
nodes.rationale: The warning is 'unused workspace dependency pool-control'; spec 0003 asks for the line now and no note in spec 0001 or AGENTS.md records the exception. Suggested fix: take the line out and let scope 004 add it in the commit that adds the first use (one sentence less in spec 0003), or keep it and add a dated note where the rule lives.The warning fails no check, so it will sit in the output of every check until scope 004, and a warning that is always there teaches people to stop reading warnings. A spec that orders what the root guide forbids leaves the next agent to guess which one wins. Rule W5 reads the manifests of the members and does not need the line. Owner: the architect to choose, the developer to apply.

nodes.rationale: Adding Instant::now() to crates/pool-control/src/ would fail no test and no guard today. Suggested fix: when scope 004 decides where the journal reader lives, make the grep a guard, for example a list of patterns for the rule modules only; that is a change to rule W3 and needs a sentence in the spec.That pool-control reads no clock and no file is what makes the four walks run as tests and what scope 004 builds on. Scope 004 puts the journal reader into this crate, which is exactly when a file read or a clock read is most likely to slip into the rule functions. Owner: the architect of scope 004.

nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 15 (heavy): missing evidence about a replica does not close writes, only a positive conflict does, and bootstrap needs every node once; runner up: every node must be fresh for a write
nodes.rationale: Applying fail closed to every node would let the least reliable replica decide the availability of the primary.

nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 17 (heavy): a quarantined node that says it is a primary does not close writes; runner up: it does
nodes.rationale: A fenced former primary is exactly the node most likely to misbehave; it must not hold the cluster after an operation that was done right.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 1 (heavy): scope 003 builds configuration keys and a plain authority model, the journal file in 004; runner up: build the SQLite journal now
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 1 (heavy): scope 003 builds configuration keys and a plain authority model, the journal file in 004; runner up: build the sqlite journal now

nodes.label: 0003 decision 20 (not heavy): the time of validation is a criterion, a new AC-15 with Build plan step 8; runner up: widen the rule under Keys and add no criterion, or make it a part of AC-3
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 20 (not heavy): the time of validation is a criterion, a new ac-15 with build plan step 8; runner up: widen the rule under keys and add no criterion, or make it a part of ac-3
nodes.rationale: Without a criterion nothing fails when the counting goes back to once per entry: the old rule named only the uniqueness and reference checks, so its letter was met while validate took 12 s (release) and 241 s (debug) for a valid file of 16000 nodes. A new ID is used because AC-1 to AC-6 already have recorded evidence; inside AC-3 the milestone 2 evidence would have to be taken again.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 21 (not heavy): the validation time bound covers an invalid file and a file with every entry on one line; runner up: valid files only
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 21 (not heavy): the validation time bound covers an invalid file and a file with every entry on one line; runner up: valid files only
nodes.rationale: The daemon of scope 004 runs the same function at start, and a start that hangs for minutes on a generated file with a repeated mistake defeats the 1 MiB limit. The one line shape was measured (12000 inline tables, 16 s in a release build) and is the shape where the obvious repair, a table of line starts, is still quadratic. With the runner up made input 3 goes away.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 22 (not heavy): validation time is checked by an upper limit of 10 seconds on one call, in the debug build of cargo test, on three inputs at the file limit, plus one small input whose findings come against file order; runner up: a ratio between a half size and a full size input, or a release build timed by hand in the verification record
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 22 (not heavy): validation time is checked by an upper limit of 10 seconds on one call, in the debug build of cargo test, on three inputs at the file limit, plus one small input whose findings come against file order; runner up: a ratio between a half size and a full size input, or a release build timed by hand in the verification record
nodes.rationale: A ratio divides two timings of a fraction of a second, and one pause of the machine moves it past any threshold; a run by hand is not repeated by CI. The absolute limit sits about 25 times above the correct code and about 16 times below the broken code. A test cannot interrupt the call (rule W3 allows no thread), so a regression runs for minutes and then fails; slow, and still red.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 25 (heavy): a generation may not be a metric label, only a log field or the value of a metric, which narrows what decision 12 allowed; runner up: leave generations in the label column
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 25 (heavy): a generation may not be a metric label, only a log field or the value of a metric, which narrows what decision 12 allowed; runner up: leave generations in the label column
nodes.rationale: Generations only grow, so as labels they are values without a bound, against T-12. No code changes either way, because nothing writes a metric yet.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 26 (heavy): a Ready state is tied to the configuration that confirmed it, in code now: writer_admission compares the witness again, with a new AC-16 and Build plan step 9; runner up: text only, one sentence under writer admission and a rule for the reload of 009
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 26 (heavy): a ready state is tied to the configuration that confirmed it, in code now: writer_admission compares the witness again, with a new ac-16 and build plan step 9; runner up: text only, one sentence under writer admission and a rule for the reload of 009
nodes.rationale: The checker of milestone 3 passed a state classified Ready under witness X with a configuration with no witness, and with one with witness Y, and got Open both times. The case arrives with the reload of scope 009, and the spec nowhere else relies on a later slice reading a rule. The identity of the journal was the one agreement checked only once; comparing it again costs one comparison of 16 bytes and changes no signature and no reason name. The price is a second small build step after the feature was verified and one more criterion.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 27 (not heavy): TimelineId and MonotonicTime may derive Hash and the spec now lists it; runner up: remove the derive from the code
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 27 (not heavy): timelineid and monotonictime may derive hash and the spec now lists it; runner up: remove the derive from the code
nodes.rationale: Removing the derive would be a Build plan step that deletes two words and buys nothing.

nodes.label: 0003 decision 6 (heavy): a supported backup carries the hold, reconcile gives the journal a new authority ID, and the timeline rule catches part of a raw copy; runner up: a witness file outside the journal or comparing the inode
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: 0003 decision 6 (heavy): a supported backup carries the hold, reconcile gives the journal a new authority id, and the timeline rule catches part of a raw copy; runner up: a witness file outside the journal or comparing the inode
nodes.rationale: A restored journal is correct about the past and silent about everything since; it may not speak until an operator has compared it with the present. Unsolved: a raw copy or a VM snapshot rollback with the old writer up.

nodes.label: Spec 0003 option 1 (chosen): configuration keys and a plain, tested authority model now; the journal file in 004
nodes.community_name: Spec 0003 Delegated Decisions and Workspace Guards
nodes.norm_label: spec 0003 option 1 (chosen): configuration keys and a plain, tested authority model now; the journal file in 004
nodes.rationale: What this scope can prove without input or output is exactly the part that carries the safety argument; functions over values make three way agreement checkable over 8192 cases and make closed the only accidental result. The price is an interface built ahead of its caller.

nodes.label: Core and Control Independence
nodes.community_name: Workspace Layout, Bounded Read and FIFO Limit: Shared Conventions Table: Repository proposal
nodes.rationale: Core and control use independently owned boundary types; the daemon maps control snapshots into the core route view, and a trait accepted by core can be implemented in the composition layer. This avoids a hidden core to control dependency.

nodes.label: Merge or Defer Candidate Crates (no common crate)
nodes.community_name: Workspace Layout, Bounded Read and FIFO Limit: Shared Conventions Table: Repository proposal
nodes.norm_label: merge or defer candidate crates (no common crate)
nodes.rationale: Auth, pooling, router, balancer and backend start as modules in core; health, topology, failover, recovery and admin as modules in control. There is no general common crate. Extraction needs a documented decision when a component gains independent consumers, dependency weight, versioning, ownership or build isolation needs.
nodes.source_location: Merge or defer the candidate crates

nodes.label: Data plane and control plane separation
nodes.community_name: Workspace Layout, Bounded Read and FIFO Limit: Shared Conventions Table: Repository proposal
nodes.norm_label: data plane and control plane separation
nodes.rationale: The data plane reads immutable topology snapshots and never does blocking journal work, infrastructure calls or consensus per query; control publishes snapshots only after validation.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m2 (authority.rs:18, :35): StoreProbe, StoredAuthority, ApprovedTopology and Quarantine have public fields, so any crate can build a journal value and 0003 AC-12 holds only by convention; fix: private fields or a W3/W5 line in scope 004
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m2 (authority.rs:18, :35): storeprobe, storedauthority, approvedtopology and quarantine have public fields, so any crate can build a journal value and 0003 ac-12 holds only by convention; fix: private fields or a w3/w5 line in scope 004
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: when scope 004 puts the journal reader inside pool-control, make the fields private and give the tests one constructor that runs the same checks as the reader, or add a line to rule W3 or W5 that keeps StoreProbe::Present out of every other crate; record the choice in Follow-up 4.AC-12 shows that Authority, EligiblePrimary, Closed and BootstrapPlan cannot be built outside the crate, but with a free StoreProbe that proof does not carry far: the one thing that turns into authority is the thing anyone can make. Today only tests do. The spec names the condition (the journal reader stays the only code that builds a StoreProbe) and no check enforces it. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m5 (topology.rs:399, report.rs:139): one file at the size limit (349514 empty identity entries) gives 2097084 findings, up to 251 MB of output and 539 MB of memory; fix: a BufWriter in check_config, then a spec decision on a findings limit
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m5 (topology.rs:399, report.rs:139): one file at the size limit (349514 empty identity entries) gives 2097084 findings, up to 251 mb of output and 539 mb of memory; fix: a bufwriter in check_config, then a spec decision on a findings limit
nodes.rationale: Measured with the debug build on a file of 1048574 bytes: the human format wrote 190709698 bytes in 2.5 seconds with a peak of 405 MB, the JSON format 251525214 bytes in 8.5 seconds with a peak of 539 MB; the time is linear and each human finding is one system call through the line buffered stdout lock (main.rs:77). Suggested fix: wrap the locked stdout in a BufWriter in check_config, then decide in the spec whether the number of findings gets a limit (one config.missing_key per entry with no key at all, or a fixed top count with a last line).The file belongs to the operator, so this is not an attack, but it is the same function the daemon will call at a start and at a reload, and bounded resources then means about 500 times the input. AC-15 bounds the time for the made inputs and says nothing about the number of findings. A limit changes AC-3, so it is the architect's call. Owner: the developer for the buffer, the architect for the limit.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m6 (admission.rs:238, :288, observation.rs:143): the cost of one writer admission grows with nodes times observations while the configuration allows about 13000 nodes; fix in scope 004: answer from the snapshot or index observations by node
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m6 (admission.rs:238, :288, observation.rs:143): the cost of one writer admission grows with nodes times observations while the configuration allows about 13000 nodes; fix in scope 004: answer from the snapshot or index observations by node
nodes.rationale: Each call walks every node of the file, builds two lists and walks every observation for every node of the cluster; the member check at admission.rs:257 is members times nodes. Suggested fix: when scope 004 wires it, answer admission from the topology snapshot and call the function only when the configuration, the journal or an observation changes, or index the observations by node once; say which in the spec of scope 004.With three nodes it is nothing, but spec 0003 has scope 004 call the function at every session admission and again after the backend is acquired, the root guide asks for bounded work on the data path, and the validation time rule of the spec covers validate only. Owner: the architect of scope 004.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m8 (topology.rs:456): names accept the control characters U+0080 to U+009F and direction characters such as U+202E, pinned by the test at topology.rs:894; fix: a spec decision before a name reaches any output (refuse them, or escape on output)
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m8 (topology.rs:456): names accept the control characters u+0080 to u+009f and direction characters such as u+202e, pinned by the test at topology.rs:894; fix: a spec decision before a name reaches any output (refuse them, or escape on output)
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: either refuse the whole Unicode control class and the direction characters, or say in one sentence that the list is complete on purpose and that every later output escapes names.Nothing prints a name today and the telemetry table keeps names out of default output, but scope 004 sends the backend login and database to PostgreSQL and scope 009 will show identity routes to an administrator. U+009B is an escape lead on some terminals, and a direction override makes two entries look alike on a screen. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t1 (topology.rs:688): no test fails when the config.duplicate_id check for cluster.id is removed from cross_check (all 238 tests still pass; the code is right); fix: a test with two [[cluster]] entries of one id and one pinning the order of step 6.1
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor t1 (topology.rs:688): no test fails when the config.duplicate_id check for cluster.id is removed from cross_check (all 238 tests still pass; the code is right); fix: a test with two [[cluster]] entries of one id and one pinning the order of step 6.1
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: one test with two [[cluster]] entries of the same id, and one with a repeated cluster, node and identity id in one file to pin the order clusters, nodes, identities of step 6.1.writer_admission and plan_bootstrap take the first cluster with a given id, so a repeated id would carry a second expected_writer and system identifier that nothing reads. The test reviewer rated this major; the main reviewer rates it minor because an open answer would still need the first entry, the journal and fresh evidence to agree, so losing the check would confuse an operator and not open a write. It is the first test the reviewer would add. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t3 (admission.rs:89, pool-config lib.rs:44): the compile_fail,E0451 documentation tests do not check the error code on Rust 1.100.0 (E0308 also passed) although verify.md:206 says so; fix: correct verify.md and pair each with a passing test
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor t3 (admission.rs:89, pool-config lib.rs:44): the compile_fail,e0451 documentation tests do not check the error code on rust 1.100.0 (e0308 also passed) although verify.md:206 says so; fix: correct verify.md and pair each with a passing test
nodes.rationale: The four pool-control tests are at admission.rs:89, :137, authority.rs:128 and bootstrap.rs:57; the older ValidatedConfig test (lib.rs:44) names three of what are now eight fields, so it fails for the missing fields and would keep failing if the fields became public. Suggested fix: correct the sentence in verify.md, use the update form ValidatedConfig { config_version: 2, ..valid } whose only possible error is the private field, and add a passing documentation test beside each compile_fail test that uses the same paths through the public functions.These tests are the proof of the second half of AC-12 and of the AC-3 rule that validate is the only way to a ValidatedConfig. Each still catches the real mistake as long as its snippet has no other error; a renamed field or type turns it into a test that passes for the wrong reason, without a sign. Owner: the tester, and the checker for the sentence.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t5 (pool-config lib.rs:579): LineIndex has no test of its own and nothing compares it with line_column (lib.rs:556); fix: one unit test that walks every offset of a few short texts and compares the two
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor t5 (pool-config lib.rs:579): lineindex has no test of its own and nothing compares it with line_column (lib.rs:556); fix: one unit test that walks every offset of a few short texts and compares the two
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: the texts should have CRLF, a tab, two, three and four byte characters and a length that is a multiple of 256, and the test compares LineIndex::line_column with line_column.The reviewer's probes gave the right positions, but the two functions have to agree for every offset, or a syntax finding and a value finding in the same file would count columns in two ways. Not covered through validate: a stride boundary inside a multi byte character, an offset at or past the end, a tab. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review question 1: nothing gets Open without full agreement from honest inputs; writer_admission returns Open only at admission.rs:305 and Authority is made only at authority.rs:183; three caller limits remain (m1, m2, m3)
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review question 1: nothing gets open without full agreement from honest inputs; writer_admission returns open only at admission.rs:305 and authority is made only at authority.rs:183; three caller limits remain (m1, m2, m3)
nodes.rationale: An age equal to the expiry is closed and one nanosecond less is open.There is no arithmetic that can overflow: the age is a checked_sub and the generations only compare. Probes: an expiry of zero is closed, a now before the sample is closed, a conflict in cluster b closes b and leaves a open, a cluster only the journal knows is authority.cluster_unknown.
